options.content:
**Rows per dispatch** is the effective batch size: the batch-axis rows each device execution processed, whether the server merged separate requests or a client sent them pre-batched. **Requests per dispatch** counts only the server's merging, so a client that pre-batches reads 1 there while the device runs full batches.

**Fill** is rows per dispatch over the model's largest compiled batch. Low fill on a busy model means the device is running small batches: more concurrent callers, or client-side batching, would raise throughput.

Request counts and latency cover models called through the gateway. A meta model's sub-models are called inside the worker, so they appear in the dispatch, compute and batching panels only.

targets.expr: (sum by (model) (rate(worker_rows_served_total{worker=~'$worker',model=~'$model'}[$__rate_interval])) / (sum by (model) (rate(worker_dispatch_total{worker=~'$worker',model=~'$model'}[$__rate_interval])) > 0)) and on (model) topk($topn, sum by (model) (increase(worker_dispatch_total{worker=~'$worker',model=~'$model'}[$__range] @ end())))

panels.title: Effective batch size (rows per dispatch), top N

targets.expr: (sum by (model) (increase(worker_rows_served_total{worker=~'$worker',model=~'$model'}[$__range])) / (sum by (model) (increase(worker_dispatch_total{worker=~'$worker',model=~'$model'}[$__range])) > 0) / (max by (model) (worker_model_max_batch_size{worker=~'$worker',model=~'$model'}) > 0)) and on (model) topk($topn, sum by (model) (increase(worker_dispatch_total{worker=~'$worker',model=~'$model'}[$__range])))
